page: Amazon Web Services a1.xlarge is an ARM64-based virtual server powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores using the Cortex-A72 microarchitecture running at 2.3 GHz. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, but lacks an L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the a1.xlarge in the lower tiers for modern compute workloads. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is rated as average with a score of 1488.48, while multi-core performance falls into the weak category at 5919.11. Memory bandwidth is limited, measuring 12.56 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 6.77 GB/sec for write operations. Cryptographic capabilities are supported via hardware AES, but the architecture lacks advanced vector or matrix extensions such as AVX or AMX. Geekbench testing reflects these limitations, with a single-core score of 408.0 and a multi-core score of 1245.0.

Given its hardware profile, the a1.xlarge is positioned as a cost-efficient option for scale-out workloads that are optimized for ARM architectures and do not require high memory bandwidth or advanced instruction sets. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, basic database operations, and simple containerized applications. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent performance without hyperthreading interference, though the overall resource density and processing throughput are modest compared to newer generation instances.
